keyFindings.description: The re-examination the deferred wake exists to run is dropped on every error path. Once dueRooms has taken a room out of the deferred set, documentChanged can still bail at the unlocked head read (:257-263), at the locked confirmation (:270-276), or at a failed service.Evict (:280-283, which returns an error whenever CloseRoom's flush fails), and none of those re-arms the window or puts the room back. The room is then in exactly the state rounds 2 and 3 established as the defect - behind the head, holding a connected reader's stale text - with the burst's last notification already spent, while mayEvict's comment (:315-317) says a refusal 'is a wait rather than a notification dropped', woke's (:174-178) says nothing else would ever re-examine such a room, and recordEviction's (:378-380) says the room is retried on its next notification, which is the assumption this fix exists to refute. The OnConnected sweep rescues the common cause, since a database outage also kills the LISTEN connection, but not a flush that fails on a healthy one. Fix: leave the room armed unless the re-examination reached a verdict; at the very least the three comments must stop asserting an invariant the error paths do not keep. The architect ruled this blocking: a fix that restores 'nothing re-examines a room' on its own error paths makes the round a formality, and it is the kind of hole that only shows under conditions nobody drives, which is how it got in the first time.

keyFindings.file: pull request body, ## Contract change census
keyFindings.description: The census's 'An API write is deliberately not refused' is false, and false in the opposite direction from the draft it replaced. refuseRoomBehindHead reads its cursor through appendingCursor (docs/pending_authors.go:442-448), which has two sources: the live write's own cursor from the ledger, and the context-carried room cursor. The census's enumeration method, grep withRoomCursor(, can only see the second, so the live-write append - persistence.go:203-227 takes the document lock, reads latest, then calls the gate - is missing from the table. roomBehindHead returns not-behind without taking that lock when its first in-transaction read is equal, and only ReplaceText, ApplyOps and captureLiveTextAndAuthors pre-hold it, so every other applyLive caller forks unlocked and locks only inside appendUpdateTxClass; an append by the other process in that window makes latest exceed the room's cursor and the write answers 503 DOC_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. The code is right - the refusal is correct and the caller's retry forks cold and succeeds - and the defect is the contract document. The tester's sixteen-edit measurement cited in support is POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits, which is ApplyOps and pre-holds the lock, so it never established the claim. Fix: a fourth row naming the live-write append, who meets it and its disposition, a corrected enumeration method, and the handoff saying why grep withRoomCursor was the wrong instrument - it enumerates one of the gate's two cursor sources - since replacing the command without saying that leaves the next table as likely to be wrong as this one. Both of this issue's census corrections have now overshot, in opposite directions: a table built from where an error can surface claims too much, a table built from one of two cursor sources claims too little, and each was written by someone who had just been shown the other mistake.

The two new rows do not lock what the round's measurements showed. TestTheRefusedNotificationClosesARoomThatOwesASettlement gives itself a 30 s budget (:836) and asserts only that the editor's socket ended inside it; its own comment (:821-825) names the competing path - the durable gate's three refusals two seconds apart ending in failRoomLocked - and the tester measured that path at 6.0 s with the wake unwired. 6.0 s is inside 30 s, so this row passes with the wake removed and proves only that the room closed eventually, which TestADocumentWriteOnOneProcessClosesTheStaleRoomOnTheOther already covers. Bound it below the settlement path, and attribute the close to the evictor (a second eviction line) rather than to the socket ending. TestTheRefusedNotificationClosesARoomNoSettlementWillFail is a genuine lock - unwired, the room never closes - but nothing in it asserts that the trailing write landed inside the eviction interval, and the steps between the first eviction's stamp and that write (a 50 ms log poll, a reconnect budgeted at up to 10 s, and a 503 retry loop the row's own comment says is reached) can exceed two seconds on a loaded runner, after which the notification is simply allowed and the row is green with the wake unwired. That is a silent false green rather than a flake, and it is how this row's first construction already went wrong once - the tester's own record says so. Assert the shape the row depends on: that the trailing write landed inside the window, and that the close came after the window ended.

The second row's comment says A's 30-minute settle delay means 'no settlement of A's can fire'. s.settle gates only the timer-armed path: settleLastPeer runs immediately on OnLastPeer, retrySettleSoon re-arms at a fixed 10 ms, and a mark's expiry arms its own. What makes the row safe is not the delay but Evict stopping the armed timer, plus the row's own assertion that no 'settle document' line appeared - which is a checked condition and is why this is minor rather than a hole. The comment should say what the delay does and does not reach.

The second ConsumerInfo read made the earlier branch redundant: case len(info.Config.FilterSubjects) > 0 && info.PushBound now decides from a two-round-trip-old read what the fresh read at :596-603 decides, with the identical log line. Two places answer 'someone else is bound' and a log line does not say which read it came from. Deleting the first case is the same behaviour or better, since a durable whose binder went away between the two reads would then be replaced rather than skipped for another settingsPollInterval.

The reconnect sweep runs documentChanged for every entry of service.roomLoads, and documentChanged issues currentUpdateCursor before its equality early-out, so every resident room costs a database round trip on the listener's own goroutine, with no notification decided and no wake fired meanwhile. pglisten resets its failure count for any connection that reached LISTEN, so a connection dropping just after LISTEN redials at the first backoff step and sweeps again: a flapping connection becomes sustained load proportional to resident rooms, capped at maxLiveRooms (1,000). One batched read of the swept rooms' heads, or sweeping only rooms this process already believes behind, bounds it. Also at :157-159 the comment says documentChanged 'drops a room that is no longer resident' and that such an entry costs one map lookup; documentChanged deletes nothing from roomLoads, entries go only when the document is collected, and a dead entry costs mayEvict's lookup plus srv.GetDoc.

The relay is mounted on every server, on s.lifetime(), which is context.Background() when Deps.Lifetime is nil, and waitBackground calls the relay's wait unconditionally where the old waitDelivery returned at once with no hub. So a Lifetime-less server whose SSE stream is ever subscribed leaks a hijacked LISTEN connection and two goroutines, and the func Register returns never returns. No in-tree caller hits it - cmd/dispatch and the api test rig both set Lifetime - but Register is exported.

The new 'Running more than one copy' section states the preconditions a deployment must meet before two copies ('Two things have to be true first, and Dispatch can check neither of them for you') as the signing key and the migration rule, and omits the Postgres connection budget, which this change roughly triples per process: a lease pool of eight plus two more hijacked LISTEN connections, taking one process from about 22 to about 32 and a two-process deployment to about 64 against Postgres's default max_connections of 100.

Two log-contract changes with no consumer found in this repository: the delivery listener's redial line is renamed to 'dispatch: a Postgres listener has no connection; redialing' and gains a channels attribute, and the delivery bind refusal for the standby case goes from ERROR to INFO while genuine faults keep the ERROR predicate. I grepped the repository and found only Go tests and .legion/ notes - no dashboard, alert predicate or log-derived metric - but consumers outside this repository cannot be checked from here, and a line going ERROR to INFO removes its own alarm. Worth one line in the body naming both. Also fast-follow from the pair: pglisten nil-checks OnConnected but not OnWake, so a caller that sets NextWake alone panics on the first wake.
